title: Quick question for AI Game Devs
author: Low_Imagination_9670
selftext:
I love games, and I've been building [pwned.games](http://pwned.games) party games where a TV or laptop is the screen and everyone plays on their phone. Nothing to install, guests play free, solo, vs, co-up, up to 8 people in a room.

The part I'd like your take on is the creator side. You can make a game made with Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or anything else, as long as it runs on our room kit, a small script that handles the lobby, the room code and the phone controllers. AI-made games are welcome, you just tell players if they'll see or hear AI art, music or voices. 

The deal as it stands: publishing is free, there's no exclusivity, you keep your IP, and you keep 80% of each sale after VAT and card fees, or 90% when buyers come through your own link. The first 100 creators keep 85%. What we keep is mostly for hosting and broadband.

Two questions:

1. Would you put a game on something like this, or make one for it?  
2. Is that deal clear and fair, or is something missing?

It's early and payments and most features aren't live yet, so the hard truths are most useful now.
